newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails new Russian government team.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails new Russian government team.

text.p: The United States Tuesday hailed Russian President Boris Yeltsin's new government team as a committed band of reformers led by "the greatest reformer of all" -- Yeltsin himself.
The State Department pledged to work with the cabinet unveiled by Yeltsin on Monday, which included a number of young reformists in key economic posts.

"Here you have for the very first time the new senior economic leadership of the Russian Federation, all of whom are committed reformers, and of course, led by the greatest reformer of all -- Yeltsin," spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"So we think it's a very positive sign. It's a vigorous group. It's a young group. And we're very anxious to work with that group," Burns told a news briefing.
Burns picked out Boris Nemtsov, former governor of Nizhny Novgorod, who will serve as a first deputy prime minister.

"A lot of us know Mr Nemtsov ... as one of the brightest and most capable young reformers in Russia," he said. "His reform programme was certainly one of the most impressive undertaken by any city in the Russian Federation over the last five years."

"His appointment, the fact that Anatoly Chubais is first deputy prime minister, the fact that you have in Prime Minister (Viktor) Chernomyrdin someone who has led the way to the current success ... this is a pretty good programme."
Earlier, National Security Adviser Sandy Berger said Russia should take action to make foreign investment "safer" if it wanted strong economic growth.

"There remain serious problems in the Russian economy that President Yeltsin has addressed quite forcefully over the past few days," Berger told a news conference two days before President Bill Clinton and Yeltsin begin a summit in Helsinki.

"If Russia does those things which make foreign investment safer and more stable and more secure, we believe that there is a very substantial amount of foreign investment that is interested in the Russian market," he said.
